aspectTitle: Title is a non-empty but non-identifying artifact: authoring-tool default, unfilled placeholder, or filename/code string
aspectDescription: F25 names a family of title strings that are non-empty, valid, and pass the presence rule (2779a5), yet fail 2.4.2 because the string itself identifies nothing about the page's content. Three sub-classes, all requiring semantic recognition that the string is residue rather than content: (a) authoring-tool defaults ('Untitled Document', 'Enter the title of your HTML document here', 'No Title', 'New Page 1'); (b) filler/placeholder/unfilled-template text ('Lorem ipsum', 'TODO: title', 'PAGE TITLE HERE', 'xxxxx', 'test'); (c) filenames or machine identifiers that are not descriptive in their own
scenario: A finished quarterly-revenue investor-relations article (masthead, prose, management quotes, a revenue-by-segment data table) whose <title> is the literal Adobe Dreamweaver new-document default 'Untitled Document'.
mechanism: F25 sub-class (a): authoring-tool default title. The <title> text node is 'Untitled Document', which announces the absence of a title and identifies nothing about the Q3-revenue subject; AT/tab/bookmark/search-result readers cannot distinguish it from any other 'Untitled Document'.

aspectTitle: Title describes a secondary/peripheral block instead of the page's primary topic (rich mixed-content pages)
aspectDescription:
F25 fails titles that do not identify the contents or purpose of the OVERALL page. On a realistic page with mixed content (a main article plus a sidebar, ad rail, promo banner, related-links, footer tagline), a title can be non-empty and genuinely describe SOMETHING present on the page while completely missing the page's primary subject — e.g. a detailed page about a city budget vote titled after the top promo banner ('Summer Sale - 20% Off'), or a recipe page titled after its sidebar newsletter widget. The c4a8a4 corpus only ever has a single short

as the entire body, so the page's topic
scenario: Long-form local-news article (~600 words) on the Cedar Falls City Council adopting a $214M municipal budget after a contested vote on police and parks funding. The page is a rich news layout (promo banner, masthead, section nav, article, sidebar with most-read/ad/newsletter, footer), but the <title> 'Summer Sale — 20% Off Annual Subscriptions | Cedar Falls Tribune' is lifted from the top rotating subscription promo banner — a peripheral marketing block, not the budget story that is the page's primary topic.
mechanism: F25 limb (b): the <title> is non-empty and accurately describes a real, present PERIPHERAL block (.promo-banner), but does not identify the OVERALL/primary content (the article#hl headline about the $214M budget vote). A screen reader announces the page as a sale promo; in tabs/history/bookmarks/search the budget story is filed under marketing copy, and two different stories could share the identical promo title, so it also fails to distinguish the page.

aspectTitle: Stale / copy-paste title: right subject family, wrong specific instance (date, name, version, account)
aspectDescription: F25 and Trusted Tester 12.B require the title to accurately identify THIS page. A pervasive real-world failure is a title carried over from a template clone or a prior edit: it is on-topic for the section and looks entirely plausible, but names the wrong specific item — last month's statement title on this month's statement, last year's gala date on this year's event, the donor product's name on a duplicated product page. c4a8a4's 'Apple harvesting season' on a clementine page is the only wrong-subject case, and it is a gross, obvious cross-domain swap (different fruit). The corpus has no subt
scenario: Online-banking statement view. The body is unambiguously the December 2005 statement for Account 1234-5678 (H1, statement-period metadata 1-31 Dec 2005, every transaction date 02-30 Dec 2005, closing-balance row, breadcrumb current page, PDF download filename ...-2005-12-..., footer). The <title> reads 'Meridian Bank — November 2005 statement for Account 1234-5678' — the statement template carried over the prior month's title. Mirrors the WCAG Understanding bank example run in reverse: same bank/document-type/account, plausible month, one stale identifier (the month).
mechanism: F25 descriptiveness limb (Trusted Tester 12.B): a present, on-topic <title> names a DIFFERENT (sibling) statement than the page's content. The month is the identifier that distinguishes monthly statements in a set; the title's month (November) contradicts the body's true period (December), so within the set it neither identifies this page nor distinguishes it.
